<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:differential_entropy_sign}
The integral in \eqref{eq:continuous_cycle_entropy} is a differential
entropy \cite{Shannon1948,DemetriusLegendreHarremoes2009}.
Unlike probabilities, density values need not lie in \([0,1]\), so this
integral need not be non-negative. For example, fix \(a_0\geq0\) and a
window length \(\varepsilon>0\). The uniform density on that window satisfies
\begin{equation*}
p_\varepsilon(a)=
\begin{cases}
1/\varepsilon,&a_0\leq a\leq a_0+\varepsilon,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
S_\tau[p_\varepsilon]=\log(\varepsilon/\tau).
\end{equation*}
Here \(S_\tau[p_\varepsilon]\) means \eqref{eq:continuous_cycle_entropy}
evaluated at \(p_\varepsilon\); it is negative when \(\varepsilon<\tau\).
By contrast, \(-\sum_j p_j\log p_j\geq0\) for every discrete probability
distribution \((p_j)_j\). The reconstruction results below concern the
reference-dependent differential entropy, not an identification of these
two functionals or a claim that the reconstructed entropy is non-negative.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{pro:potential_decomposition}
For the reproductive density \(p(a)=e^{-ra}V(a)\), where \(r\) satisfies
Euler--Lotka and the finiteness assumptions above hold,
\begin{equation}
r=H_\tau+\Phi_\tau.
\label{eq:entropy_potential_decomposition}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{pro:reference_scale_change}

Let \(\widetilde a=ca\), \(c>0\). Then the cycle entropy $S$, generation time $T$ and evolutionary entropy $H$ scale according to:
\begin{enumerate}
	\item[(i)] $\widetilde S=S,$
		\item[(ii)] $\widetilde T=cT,$
	\item[(iii)] $\widetilde H=\dfrac{H}{c}.$
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
From
\eqref{eq:time_unit_density} and
\eqref{eq:time_unit_reference_scale} it follows that
\[
\widetilde\tau\,
\widetilde p(\widetilde a)
=
c\tau
\frac{1}{c}
p\!\left(\frac{\widetilde a}{c}\right)
=
\tau
p\!\left(\frac{\widetilde a}{c}\right).
\]
Hence, after the change of variables \(\widetilde a=ca\), we obtain

\[
\begin{aligned}
	\widetilde S
	&=
	-\int_0^\infty
	\frac1c
	p\!\left(\frac{\widetilde a}{c}\right)
	\log\!\left(
	\tau
	p\!\left(\frac{\widetilde a}{c}\right)
	\right)
	\,d\widetilde a
	\\
	&=
	-\int_0^\infty
	p(a)\log(\tau p(a))\,da
	=
	S,
\end{aligned}
\]

\noindent establishing $(i)$.  Equation 
\eqref{eq:time_unit_generation_time} gives $(ii)$.  Finally, 
\begin{equation}
	\label{eq_EE_scaling}
\widetilde H
=
\frac{\widetilde S}{\widetilde T}
=
\frac{S}{cT}
=
\frac{H}{c},
\end{equation}
which proves  $(iii)$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:potential_unit_reference}
\label{pro:reproductive_potential_invariance}
For the same demographic process expressed in the coordinates
\(\widetilde a=ca\), with \(c>0\) and the same reference duration
\(\widetilde\tau=c\tau\),
\begin{equation*}
\widetilde\Phi_{\widetilde\tau}=\frac{\Phi_\tau}{c}.
\end{equation*}
If instead the age coordinate is fixed and the reference duration is changed
from \(\tau_1>0\) to \(\tau_2>0\), then
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
S_{\tau_2}&=S_{\tau_1}-\log(\tau_2/\tau_1),\\
H_{\tau_2}&=H_{\tau_1}-\frac{\log(\tau_2/\tau_1)}{T},
\qquad
\Phi_{\tau_2}=\Phi_{\tau_1}+\frac{\log(\tau_2/\tau_1)}{T}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
The growth rate \(r\) is unchanged by this replacement of the reference.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:entropy_potential_covariance}

	A change of temporal unit does not alter the demographic description; it merely changes the coordinate used to measure age, for example from
	years to months. By contrast, temporal aggregation replaces a
	continuous reproductive-age distribution by probabilities associated
	with age classes of different  widths. This process may discard information about
	reproductive timing within each class. The aggregation problem is the
	subject of the next section.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:translated_temporal_grids}
	All the constructions below remain valid for a translated partition
	\[
	I_j^{(h,a_0)}
	=
	[a_0+jh,a_0+(j+1)h),
	\qquad
	j=0,1,2,\ldots,
	\]
	provided all meshes use the same origin \(a_0\) and \(p=0\) almost everywhere below \(a_0\). For simplicity we take here 
	\(a_0=0\). In the constant-hazard model of
	Section~\ref{sec:constant_hazard}, however, reproduction begins at age
	\(A\), so the natural choice will be \(a_0=A\).
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:general_exact_entropy_reconstruction}

For every temporal partition for which the relevant entropies are
finite,
\begin{equation}
S
=
S_h
+
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
P_j^{(h)}C_j^{(h)}.
\label{eq:general_exact_entropy_partition}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
For \(a\in I_j^{(h)}\),
\eqref{eq:general_class_factorization} gives
\[
\log\!\bigl(\tau p(a)\bigr)
=
\log P_j^{(h)}
+
\log\!\bigl(\tau \varphi_j^{(h)}(a)\bigr).
\]
Hence
\begin{align*}
S
&=
-
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
\int_{I_j^{(h)}}
p(a)\log\!\bigl(\tau p(a)\bigr)\,da
\\
&=
-
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
P_j^{(h)}
\int_{I_j^{(h)}}
\varphi_j^{(h)}(a)
\left[
\log P_j^{(h)}
+
\log\!\bigl(\tau \varphi_j^{(h)}(a)\bigr)
\right]
\,da
\\
&=
-
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
P_j^{(h)}\log P_j^{(h)}
+
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
P_j^{(h)}C_j^{(h)},
\end{align*}
which, by \eqref{eq:discrete_Shannon_entropy},  is
\eqref{eq:general_exact_entropy_partition}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{pro:generation_time_exact_invariance}
	\label{pro:general_exact_generation_reconstruction}
	
	For every \(h>0\),
	\begin{equation}
			T
			=
			\sum_{j=0}^\infty
			P_j^{(h)}\bar a_j^{(h)}.
		\label{eq:generation_time_exact_invariance}
	\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Using \eqref{eq:class_mean_age},
\begin{align*}
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
P_j^{(h)}\bar a_j^{(h)}
&=
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
\int_{I_j^{(h)}}a\,p(a)\,da
\\
&=
\int_0^\infty a\,p(a)\,da
=
T.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:potential_exact_reconstruction}
Consider a temporal partition of the same reproductive process \(V\),
retaining its Euler--Lotka rate \(r\). Let \(P_j^{(h)}\), \(C_j^{(h)}\)
and \(T_h^{\mathrm{class}}\) be the class probabilities, within-class cycle
entropies and generation time in class units defined above, with the fixed
one-year reference. The reconstructed potential is
\begin{equation}
\Phi_h^{\mathrm{rec}}
:=r-\frac{S_h+\sum_jP_j^{(h)}C_j^{(h)}}{hT_h^{\mathrm{class}}}
=\Phi.
\label{eq:potential_exact_reconstruction}
\end{equation}
Thus the same within-class entropies and conditional mean ages that
recover \(H\) also recover \(\Phi\), provided \(r\) is retained.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:entropy_mesh_refinement}
	
	Let \(h_c=mh_f\). Then
	\begin{equation}
			S_{h_f}
			=
			S_{h_c}
			+
			\sum_{j=0}^\infty
			P_j^{(h_c)}
			E_j^{(h_c,h_f)}.
		\label{eq:entropy_mesh_refinement}
	\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Using \eqref{eq:exact_mesh_refinement},
	\begin{align*}
		S_{h_f}
		&=
		-\sum_{j=0}^\infty
		\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}
		P_j^{(h_c)}
		\alpha_{j,s}
		\log\!\left(
		P_j^{(h_c)}\alpha_{j,s}
		\right)
\\
		&=
		-\sum_{j=0}^\infty
		P_j^{(h_c)}
		\log P_j^{(h_c)}
		\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}\alpha_{j,s}
\\
		&\quad
		-
		\sum_{j=0}^\infty
		P_j^{(h_c)}
		\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}
		\alpha_{j,s}\log\alpha_{j,s}.
\end{align*}
	Using \eqref{eq:mesh_splitting_normalization} and
	\eqref{eq:discrete_Shannon_entropy} yields
	\eqref{eq:entropy_mesh_refinement}, finishing the proof.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:reconstructed_entropy_mesh_invariance}

For two nested representations of the same
reproductive process,
\begin{equation*}
S_{h_c}^{\mathrm{rec}}
=
S_{h_f}^{\mathrm{rec}}
=
S.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Multiplying
\eqref{eq:within_class_entropy_mesh_decomposition} by
\(P_j^{(h_c)}\), summing over \(j\), and applying 
\eqref{eq:exact_mesh_refinement}, we obtain

\[
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
P_j^{(h_c)}C_j^{(h_c)}
=
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
P_j^{(h_c)}E_j^{(h_c,h_f)}
+
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}
P_{jm+s}^{(h_f)}
C_{jm+s}^{(h_f)}.
\]
Equation \eqref{eq:entropy_mesh_refinement} then gives
\[
S_{h_c}
+
\sum_jP_j^{(h_c)}C_j^{(h_c)}
=
S_{h_f}
+
\sum_kP_k^{(h_f)}C_k^{(h_f)}.
\]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:general_exact_entropy_reconstruction}, both sides
 equal the continuous cycle entropy \(S\).
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{pro:generation_time_mesh_coarsening}
For two equivalent nested temporal representations,
\begin{equation*}
T_{h_c}=T_{h_f}=T.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Using
\eqref{eq:aggregation_consistent_age},
\eqref{eq:exact_mesh_refinement}, and
\eqref{eq:generation_time_exact_invariance},
\begin{align*}
T_{h_c}
&=
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
P_j^{(h_c)}
\bar a_j^{(h_c)}
\\
&=
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
P_j^{(h_c)}
\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}
\alpha_{j,s}
\bar a_{jm+s}^{(h_f)}
\\
&=
\sum_{j=0}^\infty
\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}
P_{jm+s}^{(h_f)}
\bar a_{jm+s}^{(h_f)}
\\
&=
T_{h_f}
=
T.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:evolutionary_entropy_mesh_invariance}

Let two nested representations describe the
same reproductive process and retain the within-class information
required for exact reconstruction. Then
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{h_c}
\frac{
S_{h_c}^{\mathrm{rec}}
}{
T_{h_c}^{\mathrm{class}}
}
=
\frac{1}{h_f}
\frac{
S_{h_f}^{\mathrm{rec}}
}{
T_{h_f}^{\mathrm{class}}
}
=
H.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
By
Theorem~\ref{thm:reconstructed_entropy_mesh_invariance},
$
S_{h_c}^{\mathrm{rec}}
=
S_{h_f}^{\mathrm{rec}}
=
S.
$
 Moreover, from  \eqref{eq:mesh_generation_time_class_units},
$
h_cT_{h_c}^{\mathrm{class}}
=
h_fT_{h_f}^{\mathrm{class}}
=
T.
$
Therefore
\[
\frac{1}{h_i}
\frac{
S_{h_i}^{\mathrm{rec}}
}{
T_{h_i}^{\mathrm{class}}
}
=
\frac{S}{T}
=
H,
\qquad i\in\{c,f\}.
\]
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:potential_mesh_invariance}
Let two nested temporal representations describe the same process \(V\),
with the same Euler--Lotka rate \(r\), time unit and reference duration.
If both retain the within-class entropies and conditional mean ages, then
\begin{equation*}
\Phi_{h_c}^{\mathrm{rec}}=\Phi_{h_f}^{\mathrm{rec}}=\Phi.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:corrected_entropy_continuous_limit}

Assume that \(p:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is continuous and has compact
support. Then
\begin{equation}
\lim_{h\to0}
\left(
S_h+\log h
\right)
=
S.
\label{eq:corrected_entropy_continuous_limit}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
\lim_{h\to0}
D_{\mathrm{KL}}
\!\left(
p\,\middle\|\,p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}
\right)
=
0.
\label{eq:within_class_relative_entropy_limit}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Since \(p\) is continuous and compactly supported on \([0,\infty)\), it is uniformly continuous. Let
$
\omega_p(h)
=
\sup_{\lvert a-b\rvert\leq h}
\lvert p(a)-p(b)\rvert
$
be its modulus of continuity. Then
$
\omega_p(h)\longrightarrow0
\ 
\text{as } h\to0.
$

For \(a\in I_j^{(h)}\),
\begin{align*}
\left|
p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a)-p(a)
\right|
&=
\left|
\frac{1}{h}
\int_{I_j^{(h)}}p(s)\,ds
-
p(a)
\right|
\\
&\leq
\frac{1}{h}
\int_{I_j^{(h)}}
\left|
p(s)-p(a)
\right|ds
\\
&\leq
\omega_p(h).
\end{align*}
Therefore
\begin{equation}
\left\|
p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}-p
\right\|_\infty
\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:uniform_histogram_convergence}
\end{equation}

Let
$\psi(x)=x\log x$ for $x \geq 0$,  with the usual understanding $0 \log 0 = 0$. 
Since \(p\) is bounded, so are the functions
\(p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}\).
Hence \(\psi\) is uniformly continuous on a common bounded interval
containing all their values.
 It then follows
from \eqref{eq:uniform_histogram_convergence} that
$
\psi\!\left(p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}\right)
\longrightarrow
\psi(p)
$
uniformly.

If \(\operatorname{supp}(p)\subset[0,L]\), then, for
\(0<h\le1\),
$
\operatorname{supp}(p_h^{\mathrm{unif}})
\subset
[0,L+1].
$
Therefore
\[
\int_0^\infty
p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a)
\log p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a)\,da
\longrightarrow
\int_0^\infty
p(a)\log p(a)\,da.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:uniform_reconstructed_entropy},
\[
S_h+\log h
=
-\int_0^\infty
p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a)
\log p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a)\,da,
\]
which proves
\eqref{eq:corrected_entropy_continuous_limit}.
Finally,
\eqref{eq:corrected_entropy_global_KL} gives
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}
\!\left(
p\,\middle\|\,p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}
\right)
=
S_h+\log h-S
\longrightarrow0,
\]
proving
\eqref{eq:within_class_relative_entropy_limit}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
The compact-support assumption is convenient rather than essential. The same conclusion remains valid for densities on unbounded age
intervals, provided the histogram approximations converge with adequate
control of the entropy tails. The constant-hazard model of the next section has unbounded support, but
is treated exactly and does not require
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrected_entropy_continuous_limit}.
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:corrected_evolutionary_entropy_limit}

Under the assumptions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrected_entropy_continuous_limit},
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{h\to0}
H_h^{\mathrm{unif}}
=
H.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:potential_uniform_limit}
Under the assumptions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:corrected_entropy_continuous_limit}, retain the
Euler--Lotka rate \(r\) of the original process and the one-year reference.
For the uniform reconstruction, define
\begin{equation*}
\Phi_h^{\mathrm{unif}}:=r-H_h^{\mathrm{unif}}
=r-\frac{S_h+\log h}{T_h^{\mathrm{unif}}}.
\end{equation*}
This is the potential of the net reproductive function
\(V_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a):=e^{ra}p_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a)\), which has
Euler--Lotka rate \(r\). Then
\begin{equation}
\Phi_h^{\mathrm{unif}}-\Phi
=-\bigl(H_h^{\mathrm{unif}}-H\bigr)\longrightarrow0
\qquad(h\to0).
\label{eq:potential_uniform_limit}
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:exact_temporal_invariance}
Fix \(A>0\), \(\beta>0\) and \(h>0\). 
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
	\item[(i)] $S_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(q_h)
	=
	S(A,\beta),$
	\item[(ii)] $T_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(A,q_h)
	=
	T(A,\beta),$
	\item[(iii)] $H_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(A,q_h)
	=
	H(A,\beta).$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
All the relevant computations were performed above. Substituting $q_h=e^{-\beta h}$ into
\eqref{eq:exact_cycle_entropy_q},
\eqref{eq:exact_generation_time_q}, and
\eqref{eq:exact_finite_mesh_H} yields identities $(i), \  (ii)$ and $(iii)$, respectively.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- rem-5: body_md -->
In the open-group representation,
$
q_h=e^{-\beta h},
$
so the geometric parameter $q_h$ depends on the temporal mesh, whereas the
physical decay rate \(\beta\) does not. Consequently, the raw sensitivity
$
\partial H_h^{\rm exact}/\partial q_h
$
is mesh-dependent.

Recalling that 
$
H_h^{\rm exact}(A,q_h)=H(A,\beta)$
with $
\beta=-\frac{\log q_h}{h},
$
the chain rule gives
\[
\frac{\partial H_h^{\rm exact}}{\partial q_h}
=
-\frac{1}{hq_h}
\frac{\partial H}{\partial\beta},
\]
or equivalently,
\[
hq_h
\frac{\partial H_h^{\rm exact}}{\partial q_h}
=
-\frac{\partial H}{\partial\beta}.
\]
The scaled sensitivity on the left-hand side therefore depends only on the
physical parameter \(\beta\) and is independent of the temporal mesh.

Thus, if \(h_c\) and \(h_f\) are two temporal meshes describing the
same constant-hazard reproductive process, then
\[
hq_h
\frac{\partial H_h^{\rm exact}}{\partial q_h}
\]
has the same value for both representations.

Since
$ {\displaystyle
\frac{\partial H}{\partial\beta}
=
-\frac{\log\beta+A\beta}
{(1+A\beta)^2}, }
$
we obtain
\[
hq_h
\frac{\partial H_h^{\rm exact}}{\partial q_h}
=
\frac{\log\beta+A\beta}
{(1+A\beta)^2}.
\]
<!-- end rem-5 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:potential_exponential}
Fix \(A>0\), \(r\) and the one-year reference, and restrict
\(\beta>0\) to \(\beta>r\), so that \(\mu=\beta-r>0\).
Write \(\Phi(A,\beta;r)\) for the potential of this family.
For a mesh \(h>0\), define
\(\Phi_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(A,q;r):=r-H_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(A,q)\),
where \(0<q<1\) and \(-\log q/h>r\). With \(q_h=e^{-\beta h}\),
\begin{equation}
\Phi_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(A,q_h;r)
=\Phi(A,\beta;r)
=r-\frac{\beta(1-\log\beta)}{1+A\beta}.
\label{eq:potential_exponential_geometric}
\end{equation}
At fixed \(A,r\), its sensitivity satisfies
\begin{equation}
hq_h\frac{\partial\Phi_h^{\mathrm{exact}}}{\partial q}(A,q_h;r)
=-\frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial\beta}(A,\beta;r)
=-\frac{\log\beta+A\beta}{(1+A\beta)^2}.
\label{eq:potential_scaled_sensitivity}
\end{equation}
Thus both the reconstructed potential and this scaled sensitivity are
independent of the mesh for the same physical \(\beta\).
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:continuous_critical_entropy_threshold}

For every \(A>0\), the function
\(\beta\mapsto H(A,\beta)\) has a unique global maximum on
\((0,\infty)\). The maximising decay rate is given by
\begin{equation}
\beta_c(A)
=
\frac{W(A)}{A},
\label{eq:continuous_critical_beta}
\end{equation}
where \(W\) denotes the principal Lambert \(W\)-function.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The function
$g(\beta)=\log\beta+A\beta$
is strictly increasing because
$
g'(\beta)=\frac{1}{\beta}+A>0.
$
Moreover,
$
g(\beta)\longrightarrow-\infty$
as $\beta\to0^+$
and
$
g(\beta)\longrightarrow+\infty
 \ 
\text{as }\beta\to\infty,
$
and so $\log\beta+A\beta=0$ has a unique
solution $\beta_c$. By \eqref{eq:continuous_entropy_derivative},
\(H\) is increasing for $\beta < \beta_c$ and decreasing for $\beta > \beta_c$. Thus $\beta_c$ is the unique global maximum.

Since
$
A\beta_c e^{A\beta_c}=A,
$
we obtain
$
A\beta_c=W(A),
$
proving \eqref{eq:continuous_critical_beta}.

Finally, note that  $
\log\beta_c=-A\beta_c
$, and thus 
$
1-\log\beta_c
=
1+A\beta_c.
$
Substitution into
\eqref{eq:continuous_exponential_entropy} then gives
\[
H(A,\beta_c)
=
\frac{
\beta_c(1+A\beta_c)
}{
1+A\beta_c
}
\]
which proves
$
H(A,\beta_c) =
\beta_c.
$
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:potential_minimum}
Fix \(A>0\), the one-year reference and a growth rate
\(r<\beta_c(A)\). On the admissible domain
\(\beta>\max\{0,r\}\), the function \(\Phi(A,\beta;r)\) has its unique
minimum at \(\beta_c(A)\). For every \(h>0\), the corresponding minimum
of \(\Phi_h^{\mathrm{exact}}\) is attained at the point
\(q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{exact}}\) defined in \eqref{eq:exact_critical_q}, and
\begin{equation*}
\Phi_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(A,q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{exact}};r)
=\Phi(A,\beta_c(A);r)=r-\beta_c(A).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:renormalized_discrete_threshold}

For every \(A>0\) and \(h>0\), the quotient
\[
\frac{S_h(q)+\log h}
{A+h\dfrac{q}{1-q}}
\]
has a unique maximum on \(0<q<1\). Its maximising value
\(q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}\) is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}
1-q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}
=
h
\left(q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}\right)^{A/h}.
\label{eq:discrete_critical_q}
\end{equation}
At the maximum,
\begin{equation}
\frac{
S_h\!\left(q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}\right)+\log h
}{
A+h\dfrac{q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}}
{1-q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}}
}
=
-\frac{\log q_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}}{h}.
\label{eq:discrete_critical_entropy_value}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The function
\[
q\longmapsto\frac{1-q}{h q^{A/h}}
\]
is strictly decreasing from \(+\infty\) to \(0\) on \((0,1)\), so
\eqref{eq:discrete_critical_q} has a unique solution. Equation
\eqref{eq:renormalized_discrete_H_derivative} shows that the derivative is positive before this solution and negative after it.

At the critical point,
\[
\log(1-q)
=
\log h+\frac{A}{h}\log q,
\]
and therefore
\[
S_h(q)+\log h
=
-\log q
\left(
\frac{A}{h}
+
\frac{q}{1-q}
\right).
\]
Since
\[
A+h\frac{q}{1-q}
=
h
\left(
\frac{A}{h}
+
\frac{q}{1-q}
\right),
\]
equation \eqref{eq:discrete_critical_entropy_value} follows.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:discrete_critical_threshold_limit}

For fixed \(A>0\),
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{h\to0}
\beta_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}
=
\beta_c(A)
=
\frac{W(A)}{A}.
\end{equation*}
More precisely,
\begin{equation}
\beta_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}
=
\beta_c
+
\frac{
\beta_c^2
}{
2(1+A\beta_c)
}
h
+
O(h^2).
\label{eq:discrete_critical_beta_asymptotic}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Let
\[
F(\beta,h)
=
\frac{1-e^{-\beta h}}{h}
-
e^{-A\beta},
\qquad
F(\beta,0)
=
\beta-e^{-A\beta}.
\]
At \((\beta_c,0)\),
\[
F(\beta_c,0)=0,
\qquad
\frac{\partial F}{\partial\beta}(\beta_c,0)
=
1+A\beta_c>0.
\]
The implicit function theorem gives
\(\beta_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}\to\beta_c\) as \(h\to0\).
Using
\[
\frac{1-e^{-\beta h}}{h}
=
\beta-\frac{\beta^2}{2}h+O(h^2)
\]
and writing
\[
\beta_{c,h}^{\mathrm{disc}}
=
\beta_c+ch+O(h^2),
\]
we obtain
\[
c(1+A\beta_c)-\frac{\beta_c^2}{2}=0,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:discrete_critical_beta_asymptotic}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
From \(p(a)=e^{-ra}V(a)\),
\(\log(\tau V(a))=ra+\log(\tau p(a))\) wherever \(p(a)>0\).
Multiplication by \(p(a)\) and integration give
\begin{equation*}
T\Phi_\tau=r\int_0^\infty a p(a)\,da
+\int_0^\infty p(a)\log(\tau p(a))\,da
=rT-S_\tau.
\end{equation*}
Division by \(T>0\) proves the identity.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{pro:reference_scale_change} gives
\(\widetilde H_{\widetilde\tau}=H_\tau/c\), and the same change of unit gives
\(\widetilde r=r/c\). Subtracting in
\eqref{eq:entropy_potential_decomposition} proves
\(\widetilde\Phi_{\widetilde\tau}=\Phi_\tau/c\).
For a change of reference at fixed age coordinate, use
\(\log(\tau_2p)=\log(\tau_1p)+\log(\tau_2/\tau_1)\)
in \eqref{eq:continuous_cycle_entropy} and \(\int p=1\).
This gives the stated change in \(S_\tau\), and division by \(T\) gives
the change in \(H_\tau\). Euler--Lotka does not involve \(\tau\), so \(r\)
is unchanged; the change in \(\Phi_\tau\) follows by subtraction.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{thm:general_exact_entropy_reconstruction} identifies the
numerator in \eqref{eq:potential_exact_reconstruction} with \(S\).
Equation~\eqref{eq:generation_time_class_units} and
Proposition~\ref{pro:general_exact_generation_reconstruction} identify its
denominator with \(T\). The reconstructed potential is therefore
\(r-S/T=r-H=\Phi\).
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{thm:evolutionary_entropy_mesh_invariance} states that both
reconstructed entropy rates equal \(H\). Since both representations retain
the same \(r\), their potentials equal \(r-H=\Phi\), by
\eqref{eq:potential_exact_reconstruction}.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The reconstructed density has integral one. Hence
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-ra}V_h^{\mathrm{unif}}(a)\,da=1\), and applying
Proposition~\ref{pro:potential_decomposition} to this density gives
\(\Phi_h^{\mathrm{unif}}=r-H_h^{\mathrm{unif}}\).
Corollary~\ref{cor:corrected_evolutionary_entropy_limit} gives
\(H_h^{\mathrm{unif}}\to H\). Subtracting from the fixed \(r\) proves
\eqref{eq:potential_uniform_limit}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Subtract the entropy formula \eqref{eq:continuous_exponential_entropy}
from \(r\). Theorem~\ref{thm:exact_temporal_invariance} gives
\(H_h^{\mathrm{exact}}(A,q_h)=H(A,\beta)\), proving
\eqref{eq:potential_exponential_geometric}.
At fixed \(A,r\), differentiating \(\Phi=r-H\) gives
\(\partial\Phi/\partial\beta=-\partial H/\partial\beta\).
Since \(\beta=-\log q/h\), the chain rule gives
\(hq\,\partial\Phi_h^{\mathrm{exact}}/\partial q
=-\partial\Phi/\partial\beta\).
The expression \eqref{eq:continuous_entropy_derivative} for \(\partial H/\partial\beta\)
then proves \eqref{eq:potential_scaled_sensitivity}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
At fixed \(r\), minimising \(\Phi=r-H\) is equivalent to maximising \(H\).
Theorem~\ref{thm:continuous_critical_entropy_threshold} gives the unique
maximum at \(\beta_c(A)\), where \(H(A,\beta_c(A))=\beta_c(A)\).
The assumption \(r<\beta_c(A)\) places this point in the admissible domain.
The map \(\beta\mapsto e^{-\beta h}\) is one-to-one, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:potential_exponential} preserves the values of the
potential under this map. This proves the claimed minimum and its exact
transport to each mesh.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
